questions.title: Sorted Pair Sum Exists
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int pair_exists(int a[], int n, int target)

The array is sorted ASCENDING. Use the two-pointer sweep from both ends: if the end sum is smaller than target advance the left pointer, if larger retreat the right pointer, and return 1 the moment a pair sums exactly to target (0 when the pointers cross).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, |a[i]|, |target| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Window Max Sum
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int window_max_sum(int a[], int n, int k)

It must return the maximum sum of any k CONSECUTIVE elements using a sliding window: sum the first k, then slide by adding the entering element and dropping the leaving one.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum window sum.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 1000, 0 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Prefix Range Sum
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long range_sum(int a[], int n, int l, int r)

It must build a prefix-sum table pre[i] = a[0] + ... + a[i-1] and return the inclusive sum over indices l..r as pre[r+1] - pre[l]. Use long long — the totals exceed int.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers. Line 3: l and r (0-indexed, inclusive).

Output Format:
One line with the range sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, |a[i]| <= 1000000000, 0 <= l <= r < n

questions.title: Count Set Bits
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_bits(int x)

It must return the number of 1-bits in the binary representation of x. Loop while x is non-zero, clearing the lowest set bit each round with x &= (x - 1).

Input Format:
Line 1: x.

Output Format:
One line with the popcount.

Constraints:
0 <= x <= 2000000000

questions.title: Power of Two Check
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_power_two(int x)

It must return 1 when x is an exact power of two (1 = 2^0 counts), else 0. The classic bit test: x is a positive power of two exactly when x & (x - 1) == 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: x.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= x <= 2000000000

questions.title: Max Consecutive Ones
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_ones(int a[], int n)

The array holds only 0s and 1s. It must return the length of the longest consecutive run of 1s (0 when there are none) — scan once, resetting the running length at every 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n values (each 0 or 1).

Output Format:
One line with the longest run of 1s.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, a[i] in {0, 1}

questions.title: Ride Share Pairing
questions.description:
A ride-share app pairs riders with identical destinations: two riders can share when their fare codes sum exactly to the target. The sorted code list is scanned with two pointers from both ends, counting EVERY valid pair (duplicate codes create multiple pairs). Return the number of shareable pairs.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_pairs(int a[], int n, int target)

It must run the two-pointer sweep, and when a matching pair is found count (equal left run) x (equal right run) before moving both pointers; return the total.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the number of pairs.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 0 <= a[i] <= 1000, 0 <= target <= 2000

questions.title: Monsoon Day Billing
questions.description:
A toll operator bills a partner for revenue over an inclusive day range [l, r] of a season. Build the prefix-sum ledger once and answer the billing query by subtraction.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long billing_range(int revenue[], int n, int l, int r)

It must fill a long long prefix table pre[i] = revenue[0] + ... + revenue[i-1] and return pre[r+1] - pre[l].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n daily revenues. Line 3: l and r (0-indexed, inclusive).

Output Format:
One line with the billed total.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= revenue[i] <= 1000000000, 0 <= l <= r < n

questions.title: Even Parity Sensors
questions.description:
A parity check flags sensor readings whose binary representation contains an EVEN number of 1-bits (zero bits counts as even). Count the flagged readings.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int even_parity_count(int a[], int n)

It must popcount each value (loop with x &= x - 1) and return how many values have an even bit count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sensor values.

Output Format:
One line with the count of even-parity values.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= a[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Balance Point Scan
questions.description:
A load balancer looks for its PIVOT index: the first index where the sum of everything LEFT of it equals the sum of everything RIGHT of it (the pivot value itself is excluded from both sides; index 0 has an empty left side summing to 0). Return the first such index, or -1 when none exists.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int pivot_index(int a[], int n)

It must total the array with long long, then sweep keeping the running left sum and comparing it against total - left - a[i].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the pivot index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, |a[i]| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Missing Badge Number
questions.description:
A warehouse issued badges numbered 1..m+1 but exactly one badge went missing from the recorded list of m distinct numbers. Find it WITHOUT extra memory: XOR every expected number 1..m+1 with every recorded number — all pairs cancel, leaving the missing one (a running total works too).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int missing_badge(int a[], int m)

It must fold x ^= i for i = 1..m+1 and x ^= a[i] over the records, then return x.

Input Format:
Line 1: m. Line 2: m distinct badge numbers from 1..m+1 (one missing).

Output Format:
One line with the missing badge number.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 100000

questions.title: Max Gain Trade Gap
questions.description:
A backtester scans one day's prices for the best single trade: the maximum of a[j] - a[i] over pairs with j > i AND a[j] > a[i]. Sweep once, tracking the cheapest price seen so far and the best gain; when no strictly-later higher price exists return -1.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_gain(int a[], int n)

It must keep minSoFar updated left to right, consider a[i] - minSoFar whenever positive, and return the best gain or -1.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n prices in time order.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum gain or -1.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 100000, |a[i]| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Target Length Window
questions.description:
A delivery van must cover a route segment whose cargo sums to at least target, using the SHORTEST run of consecutive stops (all values are positive). Grow a sliding window to the right; whenever the window sum reaches target, record its length and shrink from the left while it still meets target. Return the minimal length, or 0 when the whole route cannot reach target.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_window_len(int a[], int n, int target)

It must maintain a long long running sum with two pointers and return the best (minimal) window length, 0 when impossible.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n positive stop loads. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the minimal window length or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 1 <= a[i] <= 10000, 1 <= target <= 1000000000

questions.title: Bit Mismatch Count
questions.description:
A firmware diff tool compares two 32-bit configuration words and reports how many bit positions DIFFER. XOR the two words (differing bits become 1) and popcount the result with x &= x - 1.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int bit_mismatches(int a, int b)

It must compute a ^ b, count its set bits, and return the count.

Input Format:
Line 1: a and b (two integers).

Output Format:
One line with the number of differing bits.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 2000000000

questions.title: Sorted Roster Dedupe
questions.description:
A roster is sorted ascending but contains duplicates; compact it IN PLACE with a write pointer: scan once and copy an element forward only when it differs from the last written one. Return the new length; the harness prints the first len entries.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int dedupe(int a[], int n)

It must compact the array in place and return the number of distinct values kept.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted integers.

Output Format:
One line with the deduplicated values space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, |a[i]| <= 1000000000, a sorted ascending

questions.title: Container Max Water
questions.description:
Two container walls at indices i < j hold water bounded by the SHORTER wall: capacity = (j - i) * min(h[i], h[j]). Maximise the capacity with the two-pointer squeeze: start at both ends, record the area, and always move the pointer at the SHORTER wall inward. Return the maximum capacity.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_water(int h[], int n)

It must run the two-pointer sweep and return the best area.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n wall heights.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum water capacity.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 10000, 1 <= h[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Peak Subarray Sum
questions.description:
A monitoring dashboard reports the PEAK of any non-empty CONSECUTIVE stretch of the load series (the classic maximum subarray problem). Values can be huge and negative, so run Kadane's algorithm with long long: keep the best subarray sum seen and the best sum ENDING at the current index (extend the running stretch or restart at the current element — whichever is larger).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long max_subarray_sum(int a[], int n)

It must sweep once with the cur/best pattern and return best (an all-negative series yields the largest single element).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n loads.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum subarray sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, |a[i]| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Rogue Sensor Find
questions.description:
A sensor bus repeats every reading exactly twice EXCEPT one rogue value that appears once. Isolate it with XOR: folding every value together cancels the pairs bit-by-bit and leaves the rogue reading (no extra memory, one pass).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int rogue_sensor(int a[], int n)

It must XOR-accumulate all n values and return the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (odd). Line 2: n values — every value exactly twice except one.

Output Format:
One line with the rogue value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, n is odd, 0 <= a[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Dominant Vote Scan
questions.description:
A vote tally must confirm the DOMINANT option: a value appearing STRICTLY more than n/2 times. Boyer-Moore voting: keep a candidate and a counter (match increments, mismatch decrements, at zero adopt the current value), then VERIFY the candidate by counting its occurrences. Return the dominant value, or -1 when no value crosses the strict majority.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int majority_element(int a[], int n)

It must run the Boyer-Moore candidate pass, verify with a counting pass, and return the value or -1.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n vote values.

Output Format:
One line with the dominant value or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= a[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Flag Sort In Place
questions.description:
A pixel buffer holds only the values 0, 1 and 2 and must be sorted ascending IN PLACE — the Dutch national flag problem. Sweep with three pointers: everything before lo is 0, everything after hi is 2; when the mid value is 0 swap it forward, when 2 swap it back, when 1 just advance. Return via the array itself; the harness prints all n values.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void sort_flags(int a[], int n)

It must rearrange a[] in place so all 0s precede all 1s precede all 2s (no second array).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n values (each 0, 1 or 2).

Output Format:
One line with the sorted values space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, a[i] in {0, 1, 2}
